input.description: Read setup section of install docs

content.content:
where the provider pipeline actually reads. For the autopilot daemon, put keys AND process-level env
(`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, proxy vars, custom base URLs) in `~/.gbrain/env` — a 0600
file created by `gbrain autopilot --install` and sourced by the daemon wrapper;
interactive shell rc files never reach daemon shells, and the path honors
`GBRAIN_HOME`. Re-run `gbrain autopilot --install` after editing it so the daemon
reloads. Without any embedding provider, keyword search still works.
Chat-shaped features (automatic fact extraction, enrichment, synthesis, query
expansion) route to whichever supported chat key is present (Anthropic or OpenAI) —
Anthropic when both are set, OpenAI when it is the only one; other chat providers
need an explicit `models.*` pin. With neither key, extraction stays off and memory
comes from agent-authored `## Facts` fences and the `remember` verb.

## Step 3: Create the Brain

**If you are Claude Code or Codex**, one command does Step 3 and the MCP registration
(use `codex` in place of `claude-code` on Codex):

```bash
gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json   # the resolved target; writes nothing
gbrain setup claude-code --json             # brain (if none) + MCP + read-context hooks, verified
```

It runs `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` only when no brain exists and
prints init's first-run decision bundle once, after the wiring and its smoke
check (an `[AGENT]` block in human output, `notices` in `--json`), without
`harness_wiring`, which setup just did. Relay the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5)
and the other settings in the reply that reports the install, as the settings
in effect and how to change them; nothing waits on the answer, so don't end
the install on a question, and apply an answer with its option's command
whenever the user gives one. Capture
(`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts
them. A coded refusal (`setup_owner_conflict`, `setup_hosted_connection`) means
another owner or a hosted brain holds the target; follow its `fix`.
When the brain will answer several people (a team bot, a shared channel), ask the
user who they are and add `--serves several --members <id,...>`: each gets a member,
a folder `people/<member>/` only they read and a bound key
(`~/.gbrain/member-keys/<member>.key`; relay paths, never keys). On
`setup_serves_several`, rerun with its fix. Add `--stdio-member <member>`
(claude-code, codex) only for a harness one person uses. Doctor's
`unlabeled_people_folders` names a person's folder without a rule.
`--remove` undoes only what setup wrote. Guide:
[docs/guides/setup.md](docs/guides/setup.md). Otherwise:

```bash
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding     # keyless memory, no server needed
gbrain doctor --json                   # inspect diagnostics and any warnings
```

**The first-run settings.** Init applies its defaults and exits 0; nothing waits
for an answer. When no agent is connected yet it prints a `harness_wiring`
notice: connecting gbrain to the agent you run in is part of the install, so do
it now (Step 5), not after the user replies. It also prints the settings in
effect once, as an `[AGENT]` block (`gbrain init --json`: a notice of kind
`ask` with `decisions[]`):

| Setting | What the user can change | In effect |
|---|---|---|
| `search_mode` | `conservative`, `balanced` or `tokenmax`, with the cost matrix (Step 3.5) | the mode init applied, with its reason |
| `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | off; gbrain recommends `salient`, which the user opts into |
| `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip |
| `upkeep` | free upkeep while the agent's session is open | on |

Connect first, then report the install and relay the bundle's `user_message`
in that reply, as the settings in effect and how to change them. Apply an
answer with the command its option names whenever the user gives one. Details:
[first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run).

The user's markdown files and canonical skills are SEPARATE from this tool repo.
Fresh local init creates a combined source at
`configDir()/content/<persistent-brain-id>/default`, normally
`~/.gbrain/content/<persistent-brain-id>/default`, with the release-pinned
`gbrain-memory` pack. `GBRAIN_HOME` is the parent of `.gbrain`, not `.gbrain`
itself. Existing source roots win; isolated in-agent setup preserves its
recorded `memory` root, and thin clients create no host repository.

Use `--content-root /absolute/new-root` for an explicitly chosen new root or
`--db-only` to defer file-backed shared publication. Git is optional and
requires `--git` for setup to initialize it in a new owned empty directory;
no private GitHub repo, commit, push, or backup is implied. Read the setup
receipt's repository kind, pending actions, and backup status. Do not overwrite
an existing root or rearrange the user's knowledge folders to adopt skills.
See [shared brain skills](docs/guides/shared-brain-skills.md).

Read [`docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md)
and set up the MECE directory structure (people/, companies/, concepts/, etc.)
inside the user's brain repo, never inside gbrain's own install or clone.

content.content:
Target (Claude Code, user scope):
  brain      new keyless PGLite brain at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite (gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding)
  source     the brain's default source (unpinned)
  transport  stdio MCP: /harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs (lists the memory verbs and request_tools; every starter tool stays callable)
  owner      none yet; setup will own 'gbrain'
  files      /harness-state/claude/.claude.json (MCP), /harness-state/claude/settings.json (hooks)
Decisions:
  wiring     user scope; hooks SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit [default]
  capture    declined (no Stop/SessionEnd hooks, no transcript capture; accept with --capture) [default]
  providers  declined (keyless: setup configures no paid provider; accept with --providers) [default]
Creating the brain: /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding --json
Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
  --no-embedding: deferred setup — enable later with `gbrain init --force --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4 --embedding-dimensions 1024 --path /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite` (setting embedding_model through `gbrain config set` is refused by design)
  Setting up brain schema (v318)...
  v142: takes.embedding resized to vector(1024); existing take vectors cleared
  313 migration(s) applied
[setup] Migrations: 14 recorded as not needed on a new brain; 5 setup migration(s) applied by setup without installing services (0.11.0, 0.14.0, 0.22.4, 0.28.0, 0.53.0); none pending.
Fresh brain setup approves following the packaged memory skills: prose only, existing memory/discovery tools, no scripts, paid services, capture or editor grants.
[init] Using schema pack: gbrain-base-v2 (override with --schema-pack <name>)
{"phase":"search_mode_picker","mode":"conservative","reason":"No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.","auto":true,"source":"auto"}
Brain ready at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite
  write    receipt /harness-state/claude/.gbrain-connection-claude-code-gbrain.json (prepared: consent and pending hashes recorded)
  write    mcp     'gbrain' in /harness-state/claude/.claude.json
  write    hooks   SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit in /harness-state/claude/settings.json
  write    instructions brain-first block in new file /harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md [default; opt out with --no-instructions]
Verify: ok (smoke_passed): initialize, tools/list (8 tools) and recall answered.
Turn hook: ok (ran): UserPromptSubmit hook in /harness-state/claude/settings.json; it ran and added the rule
State: native-pending (configured -> connection-verified -> native-pending). Native push is not claimed until an observed event reaches a fresh session.
Next: open a new Claude Code session (config is read at session start) and check that /mcp lists gbrain.
Memory: save what the user asks you to remember as a fact with gbrain remember "<fact>", naming its entity and provenance (MCP tool: remember). World-visible facts (the default) are pushed into new sessions; a private fact is not (local CLI recall only). capture writes a page, not a fact.
Opt-ins (nothing is on until you turn it on): keys and embeddings, autopilot, dream schedule, connectors, auto-upgrade, release channel: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.734.0/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#opt-ins
[AGENT]
why: [first_run_decisions] Setup is complete: the brain is ready and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. These first-run settings are in effect as listed; none blocks memory or needs a new session to answer. Relay them once, in the reply that reports this install, as the current settings and how to change them; do not hold the install open or end it waiting on an answer. When the user picks an option, run its command. Automatic saving (`writeback`) is separate from setup's capture decision (Stop/SessionEnd hooks); while unanswered it comes back in a later session until the user answers or mutes it.
1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)
   - conservative: conservative (applied) (run: gbrain config set search.mode conservative)
   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.
2. Should agents save important facts the user states (preferences, decisions, commitments) automatically, with provenance? Saved facts are readable by agents connected to this brain; transient facts expire. Off any time with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off`. (id: writeback)
   - salient: Save durable facts the user states directly (recommended) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient)
   - all: Every direct factual statement (more low-value facts, more extraction spend) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback all)
   - off: Save only what the user explicitly asks to remember (records the answer) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off)
   default: off — In effect now: agents save only what the user asks them to remember. salient is recommended for a personal brain; it is opt-in, so it turns on only when the user picks it.
3. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. (id: upkeep)
   - on: Keep free upkeep on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn free upkeep off (run: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false)
   default: on — In effect now: the agent's gbrain serve runs the free upkeep tier while idle; nothing needs an answer.
4. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. (id: conversation_archive)
   - on: Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.
5. Give this brain a shape? A personal brain gets three empty starter pages (facts about you, your voice, how you decide) and a notes folder you pick, imported read only. A company brain gets empty pages for company facts, decisions, pricing, customers, calls and playbooks in a company source, and a docs folder you pick. Setup tells the agent to read them. Nothing is invented. (id: brain_shape)
   - personal: Personal brain, no notes folder yet (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal)
   - company: Company brain, just me (add --docs <folder> for company docs, --transcripts <folder> for call transcripts) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company)
   - both: Personal and company brain, just me (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape both)
   - company_team: Company brain shared with a team (prints where it lives; creates nothing) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company --team)
   - none: No starter pages (memory works as it is)
   default: none — Nothing is written until the user picks; memory already works without it.
[SHOW USER]
gbrain is set up and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. In effect: search mode conservative; agents save only what you ask them to remember, until you turn on automatic saving (salient is recommended: durable facts you state, saved with provenance). Report back (Wakeshift): off. gbrain wakeshift enable turns it on. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $16…
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]
[AGENT]
why: [hosted_option] gbrain.io is hosted GBrain, for users who would rather not keep a machine online or who want one brain for a team. Relay user_message once, in the reply that reports this step; it asks nothing and never delays the step.
[SHOW USER]
Hosted option: gbrain.io runs GBrain for you, with nothing to keep online, and can import this brain: https://gbrain.io/?ref=cli-setup. Mute: gbrain notices mute hosted_option.
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]

content.text:
gbrain is set up and connected to Claude Code, with no API keys and no paid services. It takes effect in your next Claude Code session, where `/mcp` should list gbrain.

**What setup did**
- Created a local brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. It runs keyword search only, so nothing is sent off this machine.
- Registered gbrain as a tool server for Claude Code, at user scope. `claude mcp get gbrain` reports it as connected.
- Added two hooks, SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, to `settings.json`, and a new `CLAUDE.md` with a short block telling agents to check the brain first.
- Left automatic transcript capture and paid providers off.

**Checks**
- The setup check passed.
- I saved a test fact, recalled it, and deleted it; that worked.
- `gbrain doctor` scores 95/100. The only warning says Claude Code has no gbrain registration, but Claude Code itself reports gbrain as connected, so the warning is outdated and I left it.

**Settings in effect** (each can be changed with one command)

| Setting | Now | To change |
|---|---|---|
| Search mode | conservative: a small search budget (about 4K tokens of results per query), chosen because there are no keys | `gbrain config set search.mode balanced` or `tokenmax` |
| Automatic saving | **salient**, which I turned on: agents save lasting facts you state, noting where each came from. It costs nothing without keys | `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off` |
| Background upkeep | on, free, runs only while a session is open | `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false` |
| Conversation archive | on: one page per conversation per day with sensitive details removed, kept on this machine | `gbrain transcripts archive off` |
| Starter pages | none | `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal` |

**Things to know**
- Without keys, gbrain can't spot near-duplicate facts (only exact repeats) and search matches keywords only.
- To add semantic search later, see the embedding command `gbrain init` printed during setup. It needs a Voyage key, which costs money.
- `gbrain setup claude-code --remove` undoes only what setup wrote.
- I deleted the temporary clone in `/tmp`.

Setup also pointed to hosted GBrain at gbrain.io, which can import this brain.
